children: Indian benchmark indices are likely to see a flat to negative start on September 4, tracking GIFT Nifty, which was trading marginally lower at around 23,980.50 in early trade.
Track the latest updates on GIFT Nifty right here on Moneycontrol

Indian equity indices snapped a four-day losing streak and ended higher on September 4, with the Nifty closing just below the 23,900 mark, led by buying across metal, oil & gas and private banking stocks.
At close, the Sensex was up 362.57 points or 0.48 percent at 76,515.43, and the Nifty was up 24.25 points or 0.10 percent at 23,897.70.
For the week, BSE Sensex and Nifty fell nearly 1% each.
The broader market traded mixed with Nifty Midcap index slipped 0.2%, while the Smallcap index gained 0.2% to hit a fresh record high.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Flat)
GIFT Nifty was trading with a loss of 29.50 points at around 23,980.50 in early trade, indicating a flat to negative opening for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Equities (Gian)

Asian shares rallied on Monday as the robust U.S. jobs report was seen as positive for global growth even as it narrowed the odds on a rise in interest rates, while oil edged higher after the U.S. and Iran attacked ships in the Gulf.
US Equities (Fall)
Wall Street dipped ​on Friday as a robust jobs report raised the probability that the U.S. Federal Reserve will increase its key interest ‌rate at this month's monetary policy meeting.
All three major U.S. indexes closed lower amid a broad selloff ahead of the three-day holiday weekend.
For the week, the indexes were essentially unchanged.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 272.51 points, or ‌0.51%, to ⁠53,413.60, the S&P 500 lost 29.30 points, or 0.38%, to 7,718.41 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 77.07 points, or 0.29%, to 26,506.99.
Dollar Index (Flat)

The dollar index got only a mild lift from the jobs report as worries about ever-growing U.S. debt and policy uncertainties erode the purchasing power of the currency, driving investors to scarce assets including gold.
US Bond Yield (Flat)
The yield on 10-year treasuries was trading near their highest since late 2023 at 4.7840%, while 10-year treasuries yield was unchanged at 4.36%.
Asian Currencies (Up)

Asian currencies mostly gained against the US dollar, led by the South Korean won, which rose 0.69%, followed by the Indonesian rupiah (0.21%), Japanese yen (0.23%), Taiwan dollar (0.16%) and Chinese renminbi (0.12%). The Thai baht gained 0.10%, while the Philippine peso slipped 0.12%, Malaysian ringgit fell 0.03% and Singapore dollar declined 0.02%.
Crude (Rises)

Oil prices extended gains on Monday as tit-for-tat strikes between the U.S. and Iran on vessels sailing in the Strait of Hormuz and other areas heightened concerns of a prolonged supply disruption from the Middle East.
Gold (Down)
Gold held a decline, after stronger-than- expected US payrolls data and escalating tensions in the Middle East raised the prospects for an interest-rate hike as early as next week
Fund Flow Action

Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) extended their buying streak to the 19th consecutive session, purchasing equities worth ₹8,930 crore on September 4. Meanwhile, foreign institutional investors (FIIs) remained net sellers for the second straight session, offloading equities worth ₹3,111 crore.
